text: Ok last question is one of the first things with the arbitrary model imports i had added was the quality slider because in general i didnt think that even any model would effectively render at all, and they do, but regardless i can still take a 400k and decimate to 4k, retain a great amount of the shape still, and this just cut a huge amount off the top. yeah?
resolution: Confirmation-only ask, no code changed. Confirmed the user's conclusion: the import quality slider (decimateExpanded, grid vertex clustering) is exactly the right lever — decimating a 400k-tri import to 4k cuts its GPU-resident vertex memory ~100x, from ~24MB to ~240KB, which lands it in hand-authored prop territory (~4x their average 980-tri model). Noted the one caveat: vertex clustering preserves silhouette well but at aggressive levels it can soften hard edges and shift UVs, so eyeball painted/hard-surface imports at the chosen level before committing; the adopted model stores the decimated result so the saving is permanent for the cooked prop.
